q-86983.name: Question 1
q-86983.problem: Which of the following is the graph of the polar curve $r=2.5\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ?$
q-86983.worked_solution:
The polar equation $r=2a\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ defines a circle of radius $|a|$ centered at the point $(a,0).$

In our case, we have $r=2.5\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,$ and therefore

$$
a=\frac{2.5}{2}=1.25.
$$

Therefore, the equation $r=2.5\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ gives a circle of radius $|1.25|=1.25$ centered at the point $(1.25,0),$ as shown below.

q-16477.problem: The polar curve $r=k\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,$ where $k$ is a constant, passes through the point $A$ with Cartesian coordinates $(-1,1).$ What is the value of $k?$
q-16477.worked_solution:
First, we find the polar coordinates of the point $A.$ The distance from $A$ to the origin is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $A$ lies in the second quadrant, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta  & =\pi -\operatorname{arctan}⁡|\frac{y}{x}| \\  & =\pi -\operatorname{arctan}⁡|-\frac{1}{1}| \\  & =\pi -\frac{\pi }{4} \\  & =\frac{3\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the polar coordinates of $A$ are $(r,\theta )=(\sqrt{2},\frac{3\pi }{4}).$ 

To find the value of $k$, we substitute the polar coordinates of the point $A$ into the polar equation of the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =k\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\ \sqrt{2} & =k\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{4}) \\ \sqrt{2} & =k(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}) \\ k & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the curve is $r=-2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,$ as shown below.
